title: Fractional-Order Spiking Neural Network
claim: Standard models describe neural dynamics with memoryless first-order components; ours generalizes them with fractional-order dynamics that capture long-range dependencies.
layout: 2 rows, left-to-right flow from brain to model; top integer vs bottom fractional
description: A two-row figure that reads left to right. On the far left is a brain illustration with labeled regions (Cerebral Cortex, Cerebellum, Occipital Lobe, Brainstem). From the cortex, arrows lead to a pyramidal neuron drawing. The top row zooms into a synapse (synaptic membrane potential). Block arrows then lead to an integer-order RC circuit (one capacitor, one resistor, one battery), and then to a leaky integrate-and-fire diagram. In that diagram, circles for H, U, S and X are linked by green charge arrows, red fire arrows and blue reset arrows, and only adjacent time steps connect. The bottom row zooms into the soma membrane with ion channels. It leads to a fractional-order RC circuit with several parallel branches and variable elements, then to a fractional LIF diagram. In that diagram, dashed and dotted arrows connect many past time steps. Bold serif captions label each stage.
caption: Comparison of traditional SNN and f-SNN framework.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) draw inspiration from biological neurons to enable brain-like computation, demonstrating effectiveness in processing temporal information with energy efficiency and biological realism. Most existing SNNs are based on neural dynamics such as the (leaky) integrate-and-fire (IF/LIF) models, which are described by first-order ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with Markovian characteristics. This means the potential state at any time depends solely on its immediate past value, potentially limiting network expressiveness. Empirical studies of real neurons, however, reveal long-range correlations and fractal dendritic structures, suggesting non-Markovian behavior better modeled by fractional-order ODEs. Motivated by this, we propose a fractional-order spiking neural network (f-SNN) framework that strictly generalizes integer-order SNNs and captures long-term dependencies in membrane potential and spike trains via fractional dynamics, enabling richer temporal patterns. We further release an open-source toolbox, spikeDE, to support the f-SNN framework across diverse architectures and real-world tasks. Experimentally, fractional adaptations of established SNNs into the f-SNN framework achieve superior accuracy, comparable energy efficiency, and improved robustness to noise, underscoring the promise of f-SNNs as an effective extension of traditional SNNs.
